# URLCode forms

> Operator-installed declarative HTML form flows for URLCode. Renders escaped
> fields through `urlcode-ui`, admits only bounded URL-encoded POST bodies,
> validates declared fields, returns 422 with field errors, and redirects a
> valid submission to a confirmation page that shows only opted-in fields. Released as a tarball on core's
> GitHub Release and installed with `urlcode extensions add forms`; only core is
> on npm. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.ui: { version: "1", config: {} }` (required; must be declared before `forms`)
- `extensions.forms: { version: "1", config: { flows: { <name>: { mount, fields, ... } } } }`
- A mount for each flow, e.g. `/contact: { extension: forms, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST] }`
- `auth: true` on a flow to require a session before the form handler runs
- The operator activates it with `forms()` in the site's `host.mjs` `composeHost` list (the
  scaffold writes that line and `data/forms-csrf.key`); `forms({csrfSecret})` or
  `forms({csrfSecretFile})` supplies the secret another way.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): activation, flow declaration, CSRF secret, the `onSubmit` hook.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md): trust boundary; what the extension does not protect.

## Do not guess
- No form-handling code in project `function`/`middleware` routes; declare the
  flow. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no forms authority
  of their own.
- The supplied `onSubmit` hook is trusted project code, runs only after CSRF
  and field validation, and should make external effects idempotent.
- Fields are escaped and rendered through the `ui` kit; there is no arbitrary
  template engine here. The confirmation shows a submitted value only when its
  field is listed in `confirmation.show`; `{field}` placeholders in its message
  must name listed fields, and a refresh shows the fixed page.
- "Required only when another field has value X" is declared, not coded:
  `requiredWhen: {field: <sibling select or enum field>, in: [values]}` on the
  dependent field, without `required`. One level only, checked at startup,
  enforced by the server (422 `is required`). AND/OR, not-equal, comparisons,
  cross-field ordering, conditions on free-text fields and show/hide still
  belong in `onSubmit`.
